title: [observability] The drills tests that run a fake systemctl pass every time: no exec of a fake fails on a busy file, and no two tests share a scratch directory (the flaky check-tests row of task 328's gate)
prompt:
Read crates/spawn-cli/src/serve/core_lines/drills.rs (its tests: script(), the fake systemctl, Scratch, a_refused_name_is_never_run) and crates/spawn-cli/src/storage.rs (tests::scratch).

The record. Flake Doctor's real page on FD 016 has the row `flaky check-tests.sh 086ea501 4bedc797 … serve::core_lines::drills::tests::a_unit_call_that_runs_over_is_killed_and_no_pass`. In task 328's own gate (judging 01a1d225e6287ca96c5efb6ce7e1, unit spawn-gate-1121880-18e770dae00254de-0, stdout line 116), the test failed with `…/systemctl: Text file busy (os error 26)` at drills.rs:957, and its rerun passed. The gate log proves the errno. It does not show which process held the fake open for writing, so the historical failure's holder is not identified.

Two defects, each by what was observed. These are rev-b's measurements of 2026-11-13 on main 7df39d62: the four tests that run a fake systemctl, 16 threads, load about 6, 150 runs each.
- A, a busy fake. script() writes the fake in the test process, and the test then execs it. A descriptor open for writing on the fake, held by another process while the test execs it, fails the exec with ETXTBSY. The candidate holder is another test thread's child, between its fork and its exec. Busy failures: 10 of 150 runs on main; 18 of 150 with a scratch directory unique per test; 0 of 150 with the fake written by a child process.
- B, a shared scratch directory. Two tests got one directory, so one ran the other's fake. a_unit_call_that_runs_over answered Ok("Result=success\nExecMainStatus=0\nExecMainExitTimestamp=@5\n"), which is a_unit_call_is_argv's output. Under the gate's sandbox, a_unit_call_whose_child_holds_the_output answered Err("ran over 300 ms"), which is the runs-over test's fake. storage.rs's tests::scratch names a directory by the pid, the clock's nanoseconds and the case, and makes it with create_dir_all, so a name taken twice is silently shared. Every drills test passes the case "drills". B appeared in 1 to 4 runs of 150, and in 0 of 150 with a name unique per test.
- With both fixed (rev-b's throwaway), 300 runs had 0 failures.

Required behaviour: the drills tests that run a fake systemctl pass every time, however they are scheduled beside each other.
- No exec of a fake fails because some descriptor is open for writing on it. Either the fake is made so that no descriptor of the test process is ever open for writing on it when any test execs, or the run retries on exactly that error (ETXTBSY), bounded, and on nothing else. A retry around a whole test is not a fix.
- tests::scratch gives every call a directory of its own. A name that is already taken fails loudly; it is never shared. Make the last component with create_dir, not create_dir_all.
- a_refused_name_is_never_run asserts the good-name call's result, not `let _ =`. The test depends on that call, so a failure there names itself instead of showing up later as "ran missing".
- show() and every non-test path are unchanged. No test is skipped, removed or renamed: a renamed test is a dropped test to the gate (task 328 was rejected for one).

Files (expected; no other open objective touches them): crates/spawn-cli/src/serve/core_lines/drills.rs (tests only) and crates/spawn-cli/src/storage.rs (tests::scratch only). One crate, about 30 changed lines.
Other spawn-cli tests that set a mode were checked, and none of them executes what it wrote. integrate/judging.rs:484, storage.rs:324 and integrate/database_tests.rs:1758 set a directory's mode. database_tests.rs's world() writes gate.sh with no mode, and the integrator runs it with sh: a file opened for reading is never busy. Nothing outside spawn-cli is in scope.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/107.sh. The spawn-cli tests are built first (not judged). Then the four tests that run a fake systemctl run together, --test-threads=16, 96 times, each run with a TMPDIR of its own. (1) Every run passes: a failure of any kind fails it. This is a statistical check. On main, 7 to 12 runs in 100 fail, so 96 runs pass on the base about 1 time in 1,000 at the lowest measured rate. Under the gate's sandbox, the base failed 5 of 5 times (at runs 1, 4, 10, 13 and 14), and the throwaway passed 4 of 4 times, about 30 s each after the build. With only A fixed, it failed 2 of 3 times (B); with only B fixed, 3 of 3 (A).
Note for the lead, not a mechanism: 107.sh is a candidate to leave the gate once the helper has held for 20 landings.
check-tests.sh and check-clippy.sh must pass, and 105 must keep passing.
